The FOMC statement emphasizes a strong labor market, moderate growth, soft business fixed investment, and inflation running below 2 percent, with a risk‑management posture that keeps the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent and uses IOER/ON RRP to implement the stance. Incorporating the April 2019 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) tilts the assessment more dovish: banks reported tighter standards for C&I loans and for construction and land development loans, and tightened other terms across firm sizes; demand was weaker for HELOCs, credit card, and other consumer loans, while demand for auto and subprime mortgages was unchanged. This points to some softening in credit supply and demand, reinforcing downside risks to business investment and certain consumer credit categories. While the banking system appears resilient, the SLOOS evidence supports a more cautious bias than the statement alone.

Adjusting for SLOOS, the tone shifts modestly further dovish.
